title: ir says /er/
parentNote: Today is the first time this course says that one sound has two spellings: ir says er, exactly the same sound your child met yesterday, as in bird, girl and shirt. Children usually find this outrageous, and they are right — but reading is the easy direction, and that is all we are doing today. Both spellings say er, so both are read the same way. The slip to listen for is the i trying to say something: bird coming out as bid, or as byrd with the i saying its name. Cover the b and the d, point at the ir on its own and say er, then let them put the word back together. If they ask how to know which spelling to write, say honestly that you have to remember that one, and that nobody is asking them to write it yet.

activities.mouthCue: Exactly the same as er: curl your tongue back and say er. The letters changed, the sound did not.
activities.prompt: A new spelling and no new sound. ir says er, just like the er you met yesterday.

activities.title: The shirt in the fir tree
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Meg left her red shirt on the grass in the sun.
After dinner, the shirt is not on the grass.
Meg and her sister did hunt for it, and did not spot it.
Then Jen did spot it, up in the fir tree.
A big bird did drag it up and did stuff it in a nest.
In the nest are three eggs, and the bird did chirp at Meg.
Meg did not get her shirt back.
But Meg did grin. A shirt is just a shirt, and that nest is the best.
